verdict: 4 failures on local Chrome, none flaky (all failed both attempts): one clear test bug in the size-chart row selector, a 502 from /api/product, and two product-info mismatches (price and stock) that may come from that 502 or from stale test data.

failures.test: Product extras › the size chart switches between inches and centimetres
failures.summary: The locator `rowM` targets the L row (/^L\b/) but asserts the M row's length value (27.5).
failures.evidence: Locator getByRole('row', { name: /^L\b/ }) received "L40.5288.75"; the snapshot has row "M 39 27.5 8.5", and the later 69.9 cm check equals 27.5 in, which is also M.
failures.next_step: Change the regex on line 12 of product-extras.spec.ts to /^M\b/, or keep L and expect 28 / 71.1.

failures.summary: The local target's /api/product endpoint returns 502 on both attempts.
failures.next_step: Check the localhost:3100 server logs and upstream product data source for why /api/product 502s, then rerun.

failures.test: Product info › shows the product name and price
failures.summary: The page shows £25 instead of the expected £24.99, likely stale or fallback product data while /api/product 502s; a price-rounding bug is also possible.
failures.evidence: getByText('£24.99', { exact: true }) not found; the snapshot shows paragraph: £25 under heading "Twill Overshirt".
failures.next_step: Fix the /api/product 502 and rerun; if £25 persists, compare the CMS price for products[0] and check whether the price formatter rounds to whole pounds.

failures.test: Product info › selecting a colour updates the stock for the selected size
failures.summary: Stock for Sage/S shows 11 instead of the expected 12, consistent with product data drifting from the test fixture or fallback data while /api/product fails.
failures.evidence: getByText('12 In Stock') not found; the snapshot shows paragraph: 11 In Stock with radio "Sage" [checked] and radio "S" [checked].
failures.next_step: After /api/product is healthy, verify the Sage/S stock in the source data and either reset the fixture data or update the expectation in product-info.spec.ts.
